messages:
natalie: onboarding reported broken quickstart in Cloudflare Workers: Uncaught ReferenceError: process is not defined and streaming calls fail.
cheng: yeah CF Workers have no node globals. our package ships cjs + esm + d.ts referencing Buffer/process. runtime picks wrong entry.
rachel: short-term fix idea: publish a dedicated worker entrypoint (esm) and a tiny shim. users `import 'redwood/worker-shim'` then `import { createClient } from 'redwood/worker'`.
tom: shim should be tiny: guard process, provide Buffer fallback (Uint8Array wrappers), and a fetch wrapper that normalizes retries. avoid polyfilling full node Buffer.
infra-bot: checklist created: 1) add exports map worker entry, 2) build worker bundle (esm), 3) add worker types, 4) docs quickstart snippet, 5) CI smoke test with miniflare.
cheng: typing note: our index.d.ts references NodeJS.ReadableStream/Buffer in a couple helpers. create dist/types/worker.d.ts that removes Node refs and update package.json exports types field.
rachel: streaming gotcha: CF Response.body lacks getReader in some runtimes; worker bundle will detect and fallback to arrayBuffer() for now with comment about memory cost.
tom: i'll add a tiny CI job using npx miniflare to run a one-file check that imports dist/worker/index.mjs and asserts `typeof createClient === 'function'`. cheap and fast.
natalie: docs snippet for wrangler dev:```
import 'redwood/worker-shim.mjs';
import { createClient } from 'redwood/worker';
addEventListener('fetch', e => e.respondWith(handle(e.request)));
async function handle(){ const c = createClient({ apiKey: REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const r = await c.generate({ prompt: 'hello' }); return new Response(JSON.stringify(r)); }
```
cheng: PR incoming with export map + shims + types + miniflare test. leaving a support note so triage knows mitigation. :thumbsup:
